overview: Solution Dynamics Limited (SDL) is a New Zealand-headquartered customer communications management (CCM) company operating in New Zealand, North America, and the UK. It provides a suite of cloud software platforms, professional services, and managed mailhouse operations that help organisations — governments, utilities, insurers, charities, and dental groups — compose, personalise, and distribute communications across print and digital channels. The company is transitioning from a predominantly print-and-mailhouse model toward recurring SaaS and AI-enabled digital communications software, though the print/mailhouse segment still anchors the NZ business. FY2026 (year ended 30 June 2026) confirmed the earnings base has reset sharply lower following the loss of its largest international customer, with the full year now reported.

business_model.summary: SDL earns revenue through two broad streams: (1) Services — its New Zealand mailhouse operation that prints and distributes high-volume transactional and marketing mail for enterprise B2C customers, with postage, paper, and envelopes bundled as outsourced pass-throughs at low margin; and (2) Software & Technology — its international cloud-based CCM platform (Digital Mail Centre / DMC, Composer, Autoprod, Jupiter distributed-print network) billed under SaaS subscriptions or per-document fees, plus associated managed print and logistics for international clients. Revenue is a blend of recurring (SaaS platform subscriptions, ongoing council and utility contracts) and volume-based (per-mail-piece, per-document). Capital expenditure requirements are low; the company does not capitalise software development costs.

revenue_streams.name: Software & Technology
revenue_streams.description: International CCM cloud platform revenue — SaaS subscriptions (DMC, Composer, Campaign+), per-document fees, professional services, and bundled third-party print/logistics managed through SDL's distributed print network (Jupiter) in 50+ countries. Clients include Pitney Bowes (US/UK/France/Japan distribution partner), dental groups in the UK (nGAGE), and a range of North American enterprise accounts. Pure software margin is high; bundled print/logistics component is lower margin but forms the larger share of segment revenue. FY2026 full year confirms this segment remains structurally smaller than pre-customer-loss levels.
revenue_streams.approx_share: ~40% of FY2026 H1 revenue (61.7% decline year-on-year due to loss of largest customer; was 58-65% of total in FY2024-FY2025)

revenue_streams.name: Digital Print & Document Handling
revenue_streams.description: New Zealand mailhouse operations — high-speed digital colour and mono printing of invoices, statements, rates notices, and marketing mail for B2C enterprise clients, primarily councils, utilities, and financial services. Revenue is relatively stable but under structural volume pressure as physical mail declines. Growing digital channel (email/SMS) volumes are handled here but at significantly lower revenue per item.

revenue_streams.name: Outsourced Services
revenue_streams.description: Pass-through of postage (NZ Post bulk rates), paper, envelopes, third-party printing, and freight. SDL holds a wholesale access agreement with NZ Post and earns a margin on the spread. Margins are thin but the service is integral to the total customer solution. Revenue is growing in nominal terms due to NZ Post price increases (26% retail price rise in July 2025 on top of 15% in July 2024), but this inflates reported revenue without proportional earnings uplift.
revenue_streams.approx_share: ~48% of FY2026 H1 revenue (growing share due to postage price pass-through; was ~30% of FY2025 total)

business_model.customer_type: B2B enterprise and government — large NZ councils, utilities (water, local body), financial services, US/UK insurers and charities, UK dental corporate groups. Revenue is primarily recurring or contractual (medium-term contracts in NZ, SaaS in international). Single-site operators are not the target; SDL focuses on high-volume enterprise senders.
business_model.geographic_mix: New Zealand ~68% of H1 FY2026 revenue (up from 48% in FY2025 as international declined sharply); United States ~12%; Europe/UK ~16%; Australia ~3%. NZ anchors the business; international is the growth ambition.

main_competitors: OpenText (Exstream CCM platform) — global enterprise CCM incumbent
Quadient (Inspire suite) — French-listed global CCM vendor
Precisely (EngageOne) — enterprise data and communications software
Messagepoint — cloud CCM SaaS, similar market
Pitney Bowes — a channel partner in some markets, competitor in others (hybrid relationship)
Local NZ print/mailhouse operators — undisclosed competitor ceasing operations as of 2025 (noted by SDL as consolidation)
competitive_position.market_position: Niche specialist in global distributed print and digital CCM, particularly strong in: (1) NZ councils and utility communications, where SDL is the market share leader; (2) global postage management and distributed print across 50+ countries, where the Jupiter network provides meaningful cost savings to enterprise clients; (3) dental practice marketing communications in the UK via the new nGAGE platform. SDL is too small to compete head-on with global CCM giants on enterprise software licences, and instead positions around omni-channel solutions, postage savings, and domain specialisation.

moat_factors.factor: Integrated omni-channel platform with existing enterprise client data
moat_factors.description: SDL's clients have deeply integrated data flows (billing systems, CRM, rating systems) feeding SDL's composition and distribution platform. Switching requires re-engineering production workflows, which is costly and operationally risky, particularly for large-volume senders like councils and utilities.

moat_factors.factor: Council and utility sector relationships in NZ
moat_factors.description: SDL has built a dominant position servicing NZ local government communications, including a long-standing NZ water utility customer. The government's Local Water Done Well reforms are now materialising on schedule: five new council-controlled water organisations (including Waikato's IAWAI and Waikato Waters, Wellington's Tiaki Wai, Kaikoura-Hurunui, and Selwyn Water) went live from 1 July 2026, with a further 13 expected within the next 12 months, eventually covering three-quarters of New Zealanders across 46 councils. This is a live, near-term structural pipeline of new billing relationships, not a distant possibility.

SDL's established network of print partners across 50+ countries provides enterprise clients genuine cost savings in international mail production and postage. This is a differentiated capability relative to pure-software CCM vendors and hard to replicate quickly.

Information security certifications (ISO 27001:2022 renewed) and in-progress SOC2 certification are meaningful barriers to entry for handling sensitive enterprise billing and customer data. They are table-stakes for large enterprise clients but require ongoing investment to maintain.

SDL's software underpins Pitney Bowes' customer communications solutions across the US, UK, France, and Japan. This partner-embedded revenue is sticky (click-based SaaS growing strongly as at H1 FY2026) and provides access to enterprise accounts that SDL could not reach directly.

moat_factors.factor: nGAGE — first-mover in AI-native dental practice marketing software
moat_factors.description: nGAGE is SDL's first packaged, non-enterprise SaaS product — an AI-driven patient communications and practice marketing platform natively integrated with Dentally (a leading UK dental practice management system). Two corporate dental group customers signed by early 2026, with a stated pipeline of further groups. No independently verified update on customer count or revenue contribution has been found since the H1 FY2026 report; the FY2026 annual result (26 August 2026) should contain the most current figure but was not accessible in full detail via public web sources at the time of this refresh.

weaknesses: Extreme customer concentration — a single international charity customer previously represented roughly 30-35% of international revenue; their shift to a multi-vendor model drove the earnings collapse across FY2025-FY2026
Small absolute scale (now ~NZ$31M annual revenue post-reset, down from ~NZ$41M) limits R&D investment and sales capacity relative to global CCM competitors
Structural secular decline in physical mail volumes (NZ Post mail down industry-wide; SDL volumes falling) permanently compresses the NZ print/mailhouse business

Channel partner dependency — SDL has limited direct relationships with many end customers of its international software, relying on partners (Pitney Bowes, dental software vendors) for distribution; partner arrangement stability cannot be guaranteed
Single-site NZ production facility creates operational concentration risk

Full fiscal year (FY2026) confirms the revenue reset is not a one-off half — the business has now posted two consecutive halves at the depressed run rate, with FY2026 full-year revenue down ~24% and NPAT down ~85% versus FY2025

moat_factors: Deep integration into enterprise client billing and data workflows creates high switching costs

Dominant position in NZ council and utility communications sector, with the Local Water Done Well reform pipeline now live (5 new council-controlled water organisations operating from 1 July 2026, 13 more expected within 12 months)
Global distributed print network (Jupiter) across 50+ countries provides client cost savings unavailable from pure software vendors
ISO 27001:2022 and in-progress SOC2 certifications required by enterprise clients handling sensitive billing data
Pitney Bowes channel partnership provides embedded, click-based SaaS revenue stream growing independently of SDL's direct sales
nGAGE: first AI-native practice marketing platform natively integrated with Dentally in the UK dental market (early-stage optionality, unverified current traction)

key_risks.risk: Loss of or further reduction in revenue from top customers has proven catastrophic to earnings across two consecutive fiscal years. The former largest customer (unnamed international charity, believed to be in global health/development sector) was impacted by US and UK government funding cuts (including closure of USAid-related flows) and moved to a multi-vendor model in mid-FY2025. FY2026 full-year results confirm the impact was sustained through the full year, not just H1. Loss of any remaining top-five customer would materially alter results further.

Structural decline of physical mail: NZ Post standard retail postage rose 26% in July 2025 (on top of 15% the prior year), accelerating customer migration from print to digital. Digital email communications now approach print volumes for SDL but generate materially lower revenue and margin per item. Everything that can digitise, will digitise.

nGAGE commercial execution risk: nGAGE is SDL's primary international growth initiative. It was an early-stage product with limited customers (two corporate dental groups as at early 2026) and unproven conversion rates and churn as of the last verified update. Continued investment in nGAGE creates an earnings drag through FY2026 and likely FY2027 before meaningful revenue contribution. No independently verified customer count update since H1 FY2026 was found in this refresh.

No permanent CEO has been appointed as of September 2026. Former CEO Patrick Brand stepped down from the executive role on 31 December 2025 due to family medical issues and joined the Board; CFO Susie Watts has held the Acting CEO title (in addition to CFO/COO NZ/Company Secretary duties) for over eight months, as confirmed by the current NZX company profile. Prolonged reliance on an acting, multi-hatted CEO through a critical turnaround and nGAGE commercialisation period is an elevated execution risk.

Channel partner dependency: SDL relies heavily on Pitney Bowes (and other undisclosed partners) to distribute its software internationally. If Pitney Bowes were to internalise SDL's function, shift to a competing platform, or experience commercial difficulties, SDL's international revenue base would be materially impaired.

FY2026 full-year NPAT of approximately NZ$0.38M (per third-party data aggregators; company's own guidance range was NZ$0.1-0.6M) confirms the company is running near breakeven. Net cash remains strong (~NZ$8.4M at H1 FY2026, ~57 cents/share) but the operating business itself generates negligible profit currently. If nGAGE investment exceeds budget or the NZ business deteriorates faster than expected, SDL could approach cash consumption territory, though the buyback and dividend programme are currently being funded from balance-sheet cash rather than operating profit.
Foreign exchange volatility: roughly half of revenue is generated in USD and GBP. A material NZD strengthening would reduce reported revenue and earnings. SDL does not appear to hedge FX exposure.

Operational concentration: SDL operates from a single Albany, Auckland site for all NZ print and mailhouse production. A fire, flood, equipment failure, or site access disruption could impair customer SLAs and trigger contract penalties. SDL has a DR arrangement with a third-party printer and backup with its major equipment supplier, but this risk is not fully mitigated.

Data security and cyber risk: SDL holds sensitive billing and personal communications data for enterprise clients across multiple jurisdictions. A breach could cause regulatory penalties (NZ Privacy Act, UK GDPR), client contract terminations, and reputational damage. SDL maintains ISO 27001 and is pursuing SOC2 certification, but cyber risk cannot be fully eliminated.

Global economic and geopolitical uncertainty affecting charitable sector and enterprise IT budgets. The primary factor behind SDL's FY2025-FY2026 earnings decline was the reduction in US and UK government aid funding to SDL's largest customer (an international charity), directly connected to broader geopolitical shifts. Future government funding changes across SDL's end markets remain a latent risk.

Thinly-traded micro-cap illiquidity: SDL has under 14.5M shares on issue (falling further via the ongoing buyback) and very low daily trading volumes on the NZX. This creates significant liquidity risk for any investor needing to exit a meaningful position. The bid-ask spread can be wide and large trades can materially move the price. Market capitalisation was approximately NZ$9.0M as at early September 2026.

growth_drivers: NZ Local Water Done Well reforms: this is no longer a future pipeline item but a live, materialising catalyst. Five new council-controlled water organisations (IAWAI and Waikato Waters, Wellington's Tiaki Wai, Kaikoura-Hurunui joint organisation, and Selwyn Water) began operating from 1 July 2026, with a further 13 expected to launch within the next 12 months, eventually covering three-quarters of New Zealanders across 46 councils. Ultimately these entities are expected to bill consumers directly (like a power company), which is a structural new-customer opportunity for SDL's billing communications infrastructure. SDL already serves NZ's largest council-owned water utility.

nGAGE UK dental market expansion: SDL's AI-native patient communications platform for dental corporate groups is in early commercial rollout. Two corporate dental groups (covering 18+ and 40+ practice sites respectively) had signed as at early 2026. No independently verified customer or revenue update since then was located in this refresh; the FY2026 annual result commentary (26 August 2026) is the most current source and should be checked directly for an update before the next research cycle.

Pitney Bowes SaaS channel growth: click-based SaaS revenue through the Pitney Bowes partnership grew strongly in H1 FY2026 despite overall international revenue decline, indicating the platform relationship is healthy and scalable.

NZ market consolidation: a large NZ mail production competitor has indicated it is ceasing operations. SDL is positioned to absorb displaced customers and gain additional market share, though management has indicated it will only participate in consolidation where it delivers clear shareholder value.

Digital communications transition within existing NZ customer base: SDL is converting print-heavy council and utility clients toward omni-channel (email/SMS plus print), deepening per-customer revenue and locking in digital platform dependency even as print volumes fall.

GRI Marketing acquisition (January 2025): acquisition of a Connecticut-based marketing agency brings creative services capability and clients including The Hartford and Pitney Bowes, enabling SDL to offer unified transactional + marketing communications to North American enterprise clients.

AI-enabled software features across CCM platform: SDL is integrating LLM-based AI into DMC, Composer, and Campaign+ for document enhancement, hyper-personalisation, and analytics. Successful AI differentiation could improve win rates and retention.

Australian council expansion: SDL is pursuing Australian councils in conjunction with an Australian print partner. Australia has a similar local government billing communications market to NZ, and SDL's New Zealand credentials are transferable. Near-term contribution is modest but represents a geographic diversification.
recent_developments: FY2026 full-year result (reported 26 August 2026): Full-year revenue fell to approximately NZ$31.4M (down ~23.6% from NZ$41.3M in FY2025) and net profit after tax fell to approximately NZ$0.38M (down ~85.4% from NZ$2.62M in FY2025), per third-party data aggregation (stockanalysis.com). This is broadly consistent with management's maintained FY2026 NPAT guidance range of NZ$0.1-0.6M issued at the H1 result. This confirms the earnings reset seen in H1 FY2026 (revenue down 34.5%, NPAT down 91%) persisted through the full year rather than recovering in H2. NOTE: full announcement text, segment detail, and management commentary from the FY2026 results release/annual report were not independently retrievable via public web search at the time of this refresh — the figures above should be verified against the primary NZX announcement and annual report PDF before use in valuation.

Dividend declared alongside FY2026 result: a dividend of NZ$0.04 per share was identified (ex-dividend date 10 September 2026, per stockanalysis.com), consistent with the Board's stated intent (post-expiry of the NZTE co-funding grant in November 2025) to resume fuller earnings payout. This is a meaningfully higher per-share dividend than the FY2025 final (3.0 cents) and the H1 FY2026 interim (2.0 cents) despite full-year earnings being lower than FY2025 — implying continued distribution from balance-sheet cash rather than purely from current-year earnings. This detail should be confirmed against the primary NZX dividend announcement.

CEO remains 'Acting': as at the current NZX company profile (accessed September 2026), Susie Watts continues to hold the title 'Acting CEO, CFO / Company Secretary' — no permanent CEO has been appointed more than eight months after Patrick Brand's departure (effective 31 December 2025). This extends the leadership-uncertainty risk flagged at the last review.

Ongoing on-market share buyback through 2026: following the buyback that expired 24 March 2026 (236,868 shares acquired), a new buyback of up to NZ$0.5M began 30 March 2026 (cap of 724,147 shares, 5% of shares on issue, running up to 12 months). Multiple tranches have been cancelled through the year: 70,000 shares at NZ$0.60 (March 2026), 23,740 shares at NZ$0.55 (April 2026), 5,723 shares at NZ$0.5787 average (May 2026), and a further 20,000 shares at NZ$0.57 (reported subsequently) — around 0.1-0.5% of issued capital per tranche. Chair John McMahon has committed not to sell into the buyback. The Board continues to state the share price does not reflect the value of the business or its net cash position.

Internal shareholding restructure, not a change of control (2026): Meta Capital Limited (wholly owned and controlled by Chair John McMahon) ceased to be a substantial shareholder after transferring its entire 1,600,658-share holding to McMahon personally at NZ$0.55/share. This consolidates McMahon's ~11% economic stake into his own name rather than a company vehicle; it is a related-party administrative transfer, not new buying, selling, or a takeover signal. No takeover approach, capital raise, delisting, or share consolidation was identified.

NZ Local Water Done Well reform milestone reached (1 July 2026): five new council-controlled water organisations began operating (IAWAI and Waikato Waters, Wellington's Tiaki Wai, Kaikoura-Hurunui joint organisation, Selwyn Water), with 13 more expected within the next 12 months, eventually covering three-quarters of New Zealanders. This is the structural growth driver materialising on the timeline management had flagged, though SDL-specific contract wins from these new entities have not been separately disclosed.

H1 FY2026 result (26 February 2026, previously reported): Revenue fell 34.5% to $17.1M and NPAT fell 91% to $0.21M versus H1 FY2025 due to near-zero revenue from SDL's former largest customer. EBITDA margin compressed from 14.2% to 4.0%. Free cash flow was negative NZ$2.08M, driven by the ~NZ$1.5M mail inserter equipment purchase. Cash was NZ$8.36M with no debt at 31 December 2025.

CEO transition (effective 1 January 2026, previously reported): CEO Patrick Brand stepped down on 31 December 2025 due to family medical issues. CFO Susie Watts was appointed Acting CEO. Brand transitioned to the Board of Directors to maintain strategic and customer relationship continuity, particularly in North America.

nGAGE launch and first customers (previously reported, unverified update since): The first corporate dental group customer (18 sites) went live in February 2026. A second corporate dental group (40+ sites) signed in 2H FY2026. No further customer or revenue disclosure was independently verified in this refresh.

NZ Post postage increases (July 2025, ongoing effect): Standard medium retail mail postage rose 26% to $2.90, on top of a 15% increase the prior year, continuing to accelerate customer migration from print to digital and compressing NZ mailhouse gross margins.

corporate_actions.summary: No takeover approach, capital raise, delisting, or share consolidation was identified. The company has an ACTIVE, ongoing on-market share buyback (up to NZ$0.5M, started 30 March 2026, running up to 12 months or 724,147 shares / 5% of capital, whichever first) with multiple tranches cancelled through the year. There was also an internal, related-party transfer of Chair John McMahon's Meta Capital Limited shareholding (1,600,658 shares, ~11%) into his personal name in 2026 — an administrative consolidation of an existing stake, not a change in economic ownership or a signal of new buying/selling intent. Neither of these invalidates a standing valuation, but the buyback should be reflected in a declining share count and the cash balance should be tracked down for the cash used.

A dividend of NZ$0.04/share was identified around the FY2026 result (ex-div 10 September 2026) — larger per-share than the FY2025 final (3.0c) and H1 FY2026 interim (2.0c), consistent with continued distribution partly from balance-sheet cash given full-year earnings were still well below FY2025 levels. Confirm exact declared amount and imputation status against the primary announcement.

guidance.management_commentary: No new, independently verified management commentary from the FY2026 full-year results call/report was retrievable via public web search at the time of this refresh beyond the headline revenue/NPAT figures picked up by third-party data aggregators. The most recent verified commentary remains from the H1 FY2026 result (26 February 2026): Acting CEO Susie Watts and Chair John McMahon noted trading conditions were mixed — international performance was described as robust from Pitney Bowes SaaS growth and UK dental gains, while New Zealand faced growing margin pressure from accelerating digitalisation driven by NZ Post postage increases. nGAGE was described as a meaningful long-term value driver with expansion likely into the US and Australia/NZ beyond the UK. This refresh flags a gap: the primary FY2026 annual report / results presentation should be read directly (via NZX announcements or solutiondynamics.com) before the next valuation update, as full segment detail, updated nGAGE customer counts, and any FY2027 guidance were not accessible through general web search.

bull_case: Strong balance sheet with net cash of roughly NZ$8M+ (last verified NZ$8.36M at 31 December 2025, approximately 57 cents per share), against a market capitalisation of only ~NZ$9.0M and a share price near NZ$0.625 as at early September 2026. Shareholders are essentially getting the operating business near-free at these levels, with an active, ongoing buyback purchasing shares below cash backing throughout 2026.

The Local Water Done Well reform is no longer a future thesis but a live catalyst: five new council-controlled water organisations began billing operations from 1 July 2026, with 13 more expected within 12 months, eventually covering three-quarters of New Zealanders. SDL's existing dominance in NZ council/utility communications positions it well to win this new-entity billing infrastructure work as it is tendered.

nGAGE is a genuinely differentiated, AI-native SaaS product in an underserved niche (UK dental corporate groups, potentially expandable to US/Australia/NZ and adjacent healthcare verticals). Early traction (two groups, 58+ sites) was confirmed as at early 2026; if it scales, the revenue potential could be multiples of SDL's current software revenue, though this thesis needs a fresh customer-count update from the FY2026 annual report.

Revenue and cost base have been substantially right-sized following the customer loss (SG&A cuts through FY2025 and H1 FY2026). If any revenue recovery occurs (nGAGE scale, new water-entity wins, new international accounts), operating leverage should produce disproportionate profit uplift from a low cost base.

Consistent capital return discipline: an active buyback (up to NZ$0.5M through to March 2027) plus a resumed larger dividend (NZ$0.04/share around the FY2026 result) signal the Board is willing to return cash rather than hoard it, and Chair John McMahon (an ~11% holder, now consolidated into his personal name) has publicly committed not to sell into the buyback.
bear_case: FY2026 full-year results confirm the earnings collapse was not a one-half event: full-year revenue down ~24% and NPAT down ~85% versus FY2025 demonstrate how dangerously concentrated the revenue base is and how long a single customer loss can depress results. Any further customer loss, partner contract termination, or large client rebid could eliminate profit entirely again.

Leadership vacuum has now persisted more than eight months: Susie Watts remains 'Acting CEO' while also serving as CFO, COO NZ, and Company Secretary — an unusually heavy combined role. No permanent CEO search outcome has been disclosed. Execution risk is elevated precisely when SDL needs to convert the nGAGE opportunity and win new water-entity contracts.

nGAGE traction is unverified beyond early 2026 disclosures (two corporate dental groups). Without a confirmed update from the FY2026 annual report, the bull case for the product remains an unconfirmed narrative rather than a demonstrated inflection; a well-funded competitor or the underlying practice-management vendor (Dentally) building native marketing automation could still displace it before it reaches scale.

Structural decline in physical mail continues to accelerate: cumulative NZ Post postage increases of over 40% in two years are pushing enterprise clients toward digital rapidly, and digital communications earn far less revenue and margin per item than print, compressing NZ gross margins even where SDL retains the customer relationship.

Thinly-traded micro-cap illiquidity persists: market capitalisation of only ~NZ$9M and a shrinking share count (via the ongoing buyback) mean meaningful position building or exit remains extremely difficult without moving the price. The stock's re-rating, if any, may take a long time to be realised by outside investors given minimal institutional ownership capacity.

management.summary: John McMahon (non-independent Chair) is the largest effective shareholder, holding roughly 11% of shares — previously held via Meta Capital Limited, now transferred into his personal name during 2026 (an administrative consolidation, not new buying). His director fee was reduced to zero from January 2025 as part of the restructuring response, signalling alignment with shareholders in difficult times, and he has publicly committed not to sell into the ongoing buyback. Nelson Siva (founder and long-serving CEO, now deceased) built SDL from a NZ mailhouse toward a software-oriented business; his estate/family trusts retain a stake around 6%, maintaining founder-family alignment. Patrick Brand served as CEO from November 2021 through 31 December 2025, transitioning SDL through COVID and the post-RFP restructure, and joined the Board in January 2026 following his stepping down as CEO due to family medical circumstances. CFO Susie Watts has held the Acting CEO title since 1 January 2026 — as at the current NZX company profile (September 2026) she is still listed as 'Acting CEO, CFO / Company Secretary,' meaning no permanent CEO has been appointed more than eight months into the transition. The Board comprises five directors (four independent). Management remuneration is modest relative to peers, consistent with SDL's micro-cap profile.

dividend_profile.summary: SDL is a consistent dividend payer with a strong long-term track record (roughly 82 cents per share of cash dividends over the ten years to FY2025, or ~114 cents including imputation credits; all dividends fully imputed, a material benefit for NZ-resident investors). The NZTE International Growth Fund co-funding grant historically capped the payout ratio at 50% while active; this expired in November 2025, and the Board signalled intent to move toward fuller earnings payout plus buybacks. FY2025 final dividend was a reduced 3.0 cents per share; the H1 FY2026 interim was 2.0 cents per share (a payout well above the half's own earnings, effectively distributing balance-sheet cash). A dividend of NZ$0.04 per share was identified around the FY2026 full-year result (ex-dividend date 10 September 2026) — again larger than the period's own earnings would strictly support on a payout-ratio basis, consistent with the Board continuing to draw on the ~NZ$8M+ net cash position. This figure should be confirmed against the primary NZX dividend announcement before use. Prior peak dividends were 11.5 cents in FY2023 and 9.5 cents in FY2024. The dividend is likely to remain well below those historical peaks while the company rebuilds core operating earnings, though the strong net cash position provides ample near-term capacity to keep paying at current levels.
